scope: Controlled testnet run using one GitHub account and separate verified maintainer and contributor wallets.

issue.body:
The current source-change gate compares changed text lines. A PR can therefore edit only a Python docstring and still satisfy the implementation-change requirement.

Acceptance:
- Compare bounded Python source structurally without executing it.
- Ignore comments, formatting and leading module/class/function docstrings when deciding whether implementation changed.
- Preserve real executable or signature changes as implementation changes.
- Missing, oversized, binary or invalid source must not become an automatic pass.
- Keep ordinary added regression tests permitted, and retain the existing protected-path policy.
- Add regressions for docstring-only, formatting-only and actual behavior changes.

This is a real issue in BountyGuard's development preview. Its bounty demonstration is operated by the project author/agent using free tNEAR; it is not evidence of independent commercial adoption.
issue.title: Reject Python docstring-only edits as implementation changes

issue.body:
Project-owned testnet acceptance scenario. This Issue is reserved for a short-lived assigned bounty that intentionally receives no PR, so its original maintainer can trigger the expiry refund.

No outside work is requested. The amount is free tNEAR with no monetary value. The evidence must show that only the reward principal returns, storage/gas do not, and repeating the refund does not create another transfer.

This is an explicit test scenario, not a customer request or commercial order.
issue.title: [Controlled demo] Expiry refund acceptance; no contributor work requested
